U1: Move kafka @Rule test fixtures to a separate repository
U2: Move rabbit @Rule test fixtures to a separate repository
U3: Support admin on different platforms (Lattice, YARN, CF) with consistent REST APIs
U4: Register artifacts as libraries for include/exclude statements
U5: Named channels support to create streaming pipelines without source/sink modules
U6: Add test coverage for StreamController
U7: Prevent creating streams with duplicate names
U8: Add Kinesis module as a source module

3. Estimate effort per activity
4. Sum totals

- Create new repository structure
- Publish artifact to repository manager
- Update existing test code to use the new dependency
- Verify tests still pass

For U2 (Rabbit @Rule move):
- Extract Rabbit test fixture classes
- Create new repository structure
- Publish artifact to repository manager
- Update existing test code to use the new dependency
- Verify tests still pass

For U3 (Platform admin support):
- Design platform abstraction layer
- Implement Lattice, YARN, CF admin implementations
- Create unified REST API interface
- Test on each platform
- Documentation

For U4 (Register artifacts as libraries):
- Design library registration API
- Modify artifact registry to support libraries
- Update include/exclude statement processing
- Add validation
- Test

For U5 (Named channels):
- Design named channel feature
- Implement channel configuration
- Update stream definition parser
- Update deployer
- Test

For U6 (Test coverage for StreamController):
- Write unit tests for StreamController
- Mock dependencies
- Verify API contracts
- Integrate with build

For U7 (Duplicate stream name prevention):
- Add validation in stream creation
- Update database/repository layer
- Handle edge cases
- Write tests

For U8 (Kinesis source module):
- Research Kinesis API
- Implement source module
- Write tests
- Document

Let me estimate effort in work-hours. These are relatively large features for an enterprise framework like SCDF.

For a single developer working on this:
- U1: ~8 hours (move fixtures, update tests)
- U2: ~8 hours (move fixtures, update tests)
- U3: ~40 hours (multi-platform admin with REST API)
- U4: ~24 hours (library registration)
- U5: ~32 hours (named channels)

- U7: ~12 hours (validation + tests)
- U8: ~24 hours (kinesis module)

Plus general activities:
- Requirements analysis & design: 16 hours

- Documentation: 12 hours

technical_and_design_decisions: Reuse existing Spring Boot REST API conventions; platform-specific admin implementations expose a common AdminOperations interface so REST endpoints remain consistent across Lattice, YARN, and Cloud Foundry (U3).
Kafka and Rabbit @Rule test fixtures are extracted into a dedicated Maven module/repo, published as versioned artifacts, and consumed via a test-scope dependency in the main project (U1, U2).
Library registration extends the existing artifact registry by adding a 'library' type, allowing the stream definition parser to resolve include/exclude statements against the same registry (U4).

Named channels are implemented as first-class elements in the stream DSL with explicit channel names that can be referenced in the deployer; streams without a source/sink are represented as channel-only definitions (U5).
Stream name uniqueness is enforced at the service layer with a unique constraint on the underlying repository, returning a clear 4xx error code from the REST layer (U7).
Kinesis source module is implemented as a new Spring Cloud Stream binder module that follows the same contract as the existing Kafka source (U8).
StreamController API contract tests are added as a dedicated WebMvc/MockMvc test slice plus a contract test set integrated into the build (U6).
assumptions: The target project is Spring Cloud Data Flow (SCDF) running on Spring Framework 6.x with Java 17+.
A single experienced developer is implementing the increment; estimates are effort hours, not calendar duration.
Existing build is Maven-based and an internal artifact repository (e.g., Artifactory/Nexus) is available for publishing the extracted test fixture artifacts (U1, U2).
Admin abstraction skeleton already exists; U3 work focuses on Lattice/YARN/CF adapters and harmonizing the REST contract, not creating the abstraction from scratch.
Kinesis AWS SDK is available on the classpath; U8 implements the SCDF module on top of the official AWS Kinesis client.
JaCoCo and standard Spring Boot test infrastructure are already configured, so U6 is purely adding tests, not setting up tooling.
U5 (named channels) is delivered as a feature flag-guarded capability to avoid breaking existing deployments.
No production deployment or operational handover work is included; only development, unit/integration tests, and developer documentation.

activities.activity_description: Review all eight user stories, identify cross-cutting concerns (e.g., consistent REST contracts, artifact registry changes), and produce a high-level design covering new modules, refactored components, and build/CI impacts.

activities.activity_name: Extract Kafka @Rule test fixtures to separate repo (U1)
activities.activity_description: Identify Kafka @Rule classes, create a new repository/Maven module, move the fixtures, publish to artifact repo, update SCDF build to depend on the new artifact, and verify affected tests still pass.

activities.activity_name: Extract Rabbit @Rule test fixtures to separate repo (U2)
activities.activity_description: Identify Rabbit @Rule classes, create a new repository/Maven module, move the fixtures, publish to artifact repo, update SCDF build to depend on the new artifact, and verify affected tests still pass.

activities.activity_name: Platform admin abstraction and REST harmonization (U3)
activities.activity_description: Refine/extend AdminOperations for Lattice, YARN, and Cloud Foundry adapters; ensure REST API responses are consistent across platforms; add unit and integration tests for each adapter; update REST controllers and DTOs.

Extend artifact registry model to support a 'library' type; add REST endpoints to register/manage libraries; update stream definition parser to resolve include/exclude statements against registered libraries; add tests.

Extend stream DSL to allow defining named channels without a source or sink; update parser, deployer, and runtime configuration to materialize channels; add feature flag and tests for channel-only streams.
Add WebMvc/MockMvc unit tests and contract tests for all StreamController endpoints; integrate coverage reporting and build-time API contract verification.
Add a unique constraint/validation in the stream repository and service layer; map violations to a clear REST error response; add unit and integration tests for the duplicate-name scenario.
Create a new Spring Cloud Stream binder module for Kinesis usable as a source; implement consumer configuration, error handling, and tests; document usage.

Run end-to-end tests covering stream creation/lookup (U7), library-based stream composition (U4), named-channel deployment (U5), Kinesis source ingestion (U8), and admin REST behavior across platforms (U3).
Update reference docs and migration notes for the new repos (U1, U2), multi-platform admin (U3), libraries (U4), named channels (U5), Kinesis source (U8), and the StreamController contract (U6).
Update Maven modules, CI pipelines, and release scripts to publish the new test-fixture artifacts and to build/package the Kinesis module and any new admin adapters.
